subject: Questions about audit evidence delivery and regional bounds
messages:
From: Alice Morrow <alice.morrow@finvero.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@finvero.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Questions about audit evidence delivery and regional bounds

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing a security questionnaire for the procurement committee and have a few specific questions about Redwood's audit/access log export and retention capabilities. High-level Qs below — we've added context where helpful.

1) Retention windows: what are the default retention periods for (a) API access logs (who/when/request) and (b) tenant audit logs (admin actions, configuration changes)? Can retention be extended per-customer by contract?

2) Export capabilities: what formats do exports support (CSV/NDJSON/Parquet)? Can we get a single archive containing multiple days/regions, and is there a manifest? What is the maximum contiguous window we can reasonably request in a single export?

3) Region/residency: when we request an export for our tenant in us-west-2, will all records be scoped to that region only? How do cross-region fallbacks appear in the export?

4) Evidence of deletion: for records deleted under retention, can Redwood provide a deletion attestation (signed) or tombstone manifest we can retain for compliance?

5) PII handling: do exported logs contain raw PII? Are there options to hash or redact identifiable fields at export time?

If you can reply with short bullets and point us to an example manifest, that would be great. We may need a quick call after.

Best,
Alice
Alice Morrow
Security & Compliance, Finvero

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morrow <alice.morrow@finvero.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@finvero.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions about audit evidence delivery and regional bounds

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; I've included practical notes and next steps at the end. Attaching a small evidence_manifest_template.csv and a one-page export_instructions_v1.pdf for your procurement/legal team.

1) Retention windows
- API access logs (request-level traces): default retention 90 days for hosted tenants; can be extended to 540 days under an enterprise contract (we'll need legal/ops signoff).
- Tenant audit logs (admin/config changes): default 365 days; enterprise extensions available up to 3 years on request.
- Note: We support legal-hold overrides for preservation beyond retention while hold is active.

2) Export capabilities
- Formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and Parquet are supported for structured exports; CSV available for small slices.
- Packaging: We produce a signed ZIP per export containing: data files (by-day parquet/ndjson), a manifest.csv (file-level checksums + row counts), and a metadata.json (export criteria).
- Max window: default single export cap is 30 days for on-demand exports to control size/throughput. For larger ranges we do chunked exports (30-day slices) and can deliver a consolidated ZIP containing the slices.

3) Region/residency
- Exports are region-scoped by tenant: a us-west-2 tenant's primary logs are from that region.
- Cross-region fallbacks (rare) are included but flagged in the manifest with a region field; cross-region records are only included if they relate to requests routed via fallback.

4) Evidence of deletion
- We can provide a deletion report: for the requested retention window we return a tombstone manifest (file-level) with hashes of deleted objects and timestamps. For attestation we can arrange a signed statement (legal ops) for contract-level commitments.

5) PII handling
- Exports contain raw request metadata by default (e.g., masked usernames; we do not include request payloads unless opted-in).
- On-demand export-time transformations: we can apply deterministic hashing to configurable fields (email, user_id) or redact fields entirely. This is a per-export parameter (need to tell us fields to hash).

Practical notes / next steps:
- If you want retention increased under contract, please confirm desired windows (e.g., 540 days for access logs). We'll route to Legal + SRE for SLA/ops changes.
- For a compliance deliverable, we usually produce: (a) chunked export ZIPs, (b) manifest and tombstone report, (c) signed deletion attestation.
- I'll propose a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk the legal team through the manifest format; ping me preferred times.

Thanks — attaching templates.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Vanessa — quick internal clarification I asked to confirm before we lock the reply:

- On the PII point, can we confirm that the default "masked username" is a SHA256 hash truncated to 16 chars (we've used that pattern in other exports)? If so, call that out — legal likes the deterministic hash detail.
- For the tombstone attestation: we should reference our internal retention policy id (RET-STD-3.1) so the customer sees the policy source.

If you want me to add those two lines and resend, I can.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product, Redwood Inference

Vanessa/Marissa — that all looks good, thanks. A couple quick follow-ups:

- Please include the deterministic-hash algorithm and truncation length in the manifest (SHA256 / 16 chars) — that satisfies our privacy team.
- Can you confirm turnaround for a 1-year contiguous export (chunked) and the cost model (one-off export fee vs per-GB)? We can provide a PO if terms look right.

If straightforward, we'll ask procurement to review the export_instructions_v1.pdf and then route a PO to your finance team. If you can also add the RET-STD-3.1 reference in the deletion attestation, that would be perfect.

Best,
Alice
